question_text: Find the I.F. of the differential equation x·dy/dx − y = 2x²sec²2x by transforming it into linear form.

insider_note: P here is negative, −1/x, so the integrating factor e to the power ∫P dx = e to the power −logx simplifies to the reciprocal 1/x rather than to x itself — the sign on P is what flips it into a reciprocal.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite in linear form and identify P
steps.margin_note: One mark. Divide throughout by x to make the coefficient of dy/dx equal to 1.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing −y by x gives the negative coefficient P = −1/x — carry the sign carefully into the next step.
steps.why: Dividing every term by x makes the coefficient of dy/dx equal to 1, which is what the standard linear form requires, and it leaves a negative coefficient P = −1/x on the y term.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign on the y term when dividing, writing P = 1/x instead of −1/x.
Forgetting to divide the right side 2x²sec²2x by x as well, leaving an extra factor of x in Q.

steps.label: Find the integrating factor
steps.margin_note: The last mark. I.F. = e to the power ∫P dx; ∫(−1/x)dx = −logx = log(1/x).
steps.memory_tip: e to the power −logx = e to the power log(x⁻¹) = x⁻¹ = 1/x — a negative P always turns the I.F. into a reciprocal, never x itself.

lines.text: e to the power log A is A:

steps.why: Integrating the negative coefficient −1/x gives −logx, which rewrites as log(1/x); e raised to that log cancels back to the plain reciprocal 1/x, so the integrating factor is 1/x, not x.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign during integration and concluding I.F. = x instead of 1/x.
Writing e to the power −logx as −x by treating the exponent's minus sign as multiplying the result, instead of inverting it.
